name: Relevance
description: Measures how well the summary captures the main points of the article and whether it includes important details such as names, dates, and locations.
scale: Low (misses key points) to High (captures all key points)

name: Coherence
description: Evaluates the logical flow and structure of the summary, ensuring that it is easy to understand and follows a clear narrative.
scale: Low (disjointed and confusing) to High (well-structured and clear)

name: Conciseness
description: Assesses the length and brevity of the summary, ensuring it is succinct while still capturing the essence of the article.
scale: Low (too wordy) to High (concise and to the point)

name: Accuracy
description: Measures the factual correctness of the summary, ensuring that it does not contain any errors or misrepresentations.

name: Non-redundancy
description: Evaluates the summary for any repetitive or redundant information, ensuring that each detail contributes to the overall understanding of the article.
scale: Low (contains redundant information) to High (minimal repetition)
